text:
maria: quick sanity check — spun up speculative decode on oz-mini-v1 (4-bit q) against our toy lat/lq harness. seeing ~1.8x token/sec speedup in p95 throughput on a single GPU, latency SLO still ok for short prompts. quality: small regressions on the consensus QA set (~0.6% EM drop) and weird token-level probs on list outputs.

sam: nice, can you paste the config?

maria: sure — run was: ```
MODEL=oz-mini-v1-q4
DECODE=speculative
SPECCONF='alpha=0.25,min_tokens=2,max_prefill=16'
BATCH=dynamic
NUM_WORKERS=8
```

alex: alpha=0.25 matches our earlier microbench; curious about the "weird token probs" — any examples?

maria: on enumerations the model sometimes inserts extra commas or drops "and" at boundaries, e.g., expected: "apples, bananas, and cherries" -> got: "apples, bananas, cherries" more often than baseline. small but consistent.

june: that's likely sampling bias from early speculative branch not recovering from a wrong prefilling token. did you track when fallback happened? logs?

maria: logs show fallback rate ~3.2% of requests for long prompts (>256). For short prompts fallback <0.5%. KV cache hit ratio looked fine.

sam: can you run a tiny A/B on the SOC QA set with speculative disabled vs enabled and attach eval script? I want a diff of failure modes.

maria: starting a 10k sample A/B now. quick note: turned off temperature annealing to keep baseline consistent.

infra-bot: job 44321 queued on gpu-pool-2 (eta ~6m).

alex: also try alpha=0.15 and min_tokens=1 — reduces speculative aggressiveness. if quality recovers, it's a tuning knob we can surface in Optimize.

maria: will do. planning runs: alpha 0.10/0.15/0.25, min_tokens 1/2, run each on 10k queries.

june: let's add a targeted checklist for output formats: enumerations, dates, code blocks, JSON. those hit formatting-sensitive failure modes.

maria: added to the runlist. quick sanity patch I tried: forcing deterministic scoring on the speculative branch (score threshold + relative delta) — reduced extra-comma cases by ~30% but cost dropped speedup to 1.5x.

sam: tradeoff seems reasonable if we can flag it in the rollout. what about quantization artifacts? anything obviously different vs 8-bit baseline?

maria: not much — perplexity on eval set up ~+0.2 relative to 8-bit baseline. most quality issues map to decode path rather than quant noise.

alex: OK. next steps: (1) finish A/B and post summary, (2) run a 1000-case targeted formatting suite, (3) heatmap of fallback vs prompt length, (4) sanity audit for safety/regression triggers.

june: +1 on the safety audit. cc @eng-sre later if we see fallback spikes in prod.

infra-bot: job 44321 started on gpu-pool-2 (node gpu-09).

maria: updating thread with quick numbers once A/B finishes. low priority note: if we expose alpha as a per-route setting we might let product opt-in to more aggressive speedups for trusted routes.

sam: love that. we should document expected unit-econ delta and the quality delta for each alpha.

maria: A/B done — speculative vs baseline (10k): speed +78%, EM -0.58%, fallback 2.9%. alpha sweep results in gist: alpha=0.10 -> speed +45% EM -0.15%; alpha=0.15 -> speed +60% EM -0.28%; alpha=0.25 -> speed +78% EM -0.58%. uploading artifacts to gcs://redwood-dev/oz-mini-spec/1705554321/

alex: thanks. can you put the confusion cases (gold vs pred) into a small CSV? I'll eyeball and check whether it's a postprocessing/formatter issue vs model behavior.

maria: will do, link shortly.

june: if we surface this in Optimize, propose defaults: alpha=0.15, min_tokens=1, safety-fallback=true. note in docs that some formatting-sensitive customers should stick to alpha<=0.10.

sam: sync later today to decide canary rollout. cc @infra-bot for rollout window.

infra-bot: scheduled canary deploy 18:30 UTC -> 19:30 UTC (4 nodes).

maria: thanks everyone, posting CSV and short summary in the thread in ~15m. :thumbsup:
